Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage is dominated by two intertwined storylines: Anthropic's roughly $1.4 trillion IPO roadshow and the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which has rattled AI-sector sentiment just as hot October inflation data cements expectations of a Fed rate hike in December. Secondary threads include rising geopolitical tension around the Strait of Hormuz and its knock-on effect on winter heating costs, plus a clutch of corporate earnings and restructuring stories.

stories.headline: Anthropic prices blockbuster IPO at up to $1.4 trillion valuation
stories.summary: Anthropic launched its IPO roadshow with a $70-$78 per share price range valuing the company at up to $1.4 trillion, a figure well short of the $2 trillion once floated, as instability at key partner Nvidia added to market jitters. The offering, which could raise over $90 billion including a private placement, is seen by many outlets as a referendum on the AI boom's economics.

stories.headline: Nvidia hires Wachtell Lipton to probe Jensen Huang's alleged Chinese spy affair
stories.summary: Nvidia retained law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an independent probe into CEO Jensen Huang's affair with a woman U.S. officials believe is a Chinese intelligence asset, after the board said it had 'no reason to believe' company secrets were compromised. Huang's personal fortune has dropped over $15 billion in two days of trading, knocking him out of the world's top-10 richest list.

stories.headline: Hot October inflation data all but locks in a December Fed rate hike
stories.summary: October CPI rose 0.4% with core inflation up 0.3% for a third straight month, and Fed Governor Christopher Waller said a half-point hike should be 'considered' at the December meeting if price pressures stayed elevated, a scenario that then played out in the data. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan separately said she expects two more rate increases are needed.

stories.headline: CoreWeave earnings and Anthropic's IPO spark an AI stock rebound
stories.summary: Tech stocks were poised to jump after cloud provider CoreWeave's results reassured investors who had been nursing AI jitters, with Bloomberg noting traders piled back into the AI trade on strong CoreWeave numbers and robust IPO demand.

stories.headline: US and Iran exchange strikes over control of the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: The U.S. and Iran are waging an escalating battle for control of the Strait of Hormuz, with both sides striking islands in the waterway in recent days, prompting evacuations of U.S. aircraft from U.K. bases and energy firms like Adnoc Gas to weigh bypass routes.

stories.headline: Winter heating costs to jump 7% on average, with heating oil up 70%
stories.summary: Households using heating oil are bracing for roughly a 70% price increase this winter because the war around Iran has sharply reduced supply of that fuel, pushing average heating costs up about 7%.

stories.headline: Corporate retrenchment: PepsiCo cuts jobs, Children's Place files for bankruptcy
stories.summary: PepsiCo plans to cut about 1,000 North American jobs as it tries to revive struggling home-market sales, while separately The Children's Place filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection and is seeking a buyer by Dec. 9.

stories.headline: US soldier arrested in UK on suspicion of spying for Russia
stories.summary: A 41-year-old U.S. Army soldier assigned to a NATO rapid reaction command structure in Britain was arrested by U.K. police over allegations of spying for Russia, adding to a tense week of security headlines.

Business.gaps: Puck had no recent relevant business coverage found; Business Insider and Politico yielded no outlet-specific business/markets items beyond general political stories already excluded as off-topic.

US politics.overview: Coverage is dominated by the chaotic aftermath of the Democratic midterm landslide: House Republicans narrowly killed an impeachment push against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and both parties picked new leaders for a changed Congress (Jim Jordan for House GOP, John Thune staying atop a shrunken Senate GOP minority, while Senate Democrats publicly feud over their own direction). A second major thread is the Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang 'Chinese spy' scandal, which has triggered rare bipartisan calls for investigation, alongside continuing fallout over 2028 positioning, the National Popular Vote Compact, and the Kennedy family's lawsuit against Trump's proposed National Mall arch.

stories.headline: House GOP blocks Hegseth impeachment effort
stories.summary: House Republicans voted 211-204 to refer Rep. Thomas Massie's impeachment resolution against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth back to committee, effectively killing the effort for this Congress, though Democrats are expected to revive it once they take the majority in January.

stories.headline: Jim Jordan elected House GOP minority leader, Thune to lead shrunken Senate minority
stories.summary: House Republicans chose Rep. Jim Jordan over Majority Leader Steve Scalise to lead their diminished conference after sweeping midterm losses, while Senate Majority Leader John Thune won reelection and will become minority leader in January.

stories.headline: Rift grows among Senate Democrats over who will lead in majority
stories.summary: Sens. Bernie Sanders and Elissa Slotkin held a news conference pushing for a 'bold direction' for Senate Democrats, exposing tensions over the party's leadership heading into its new majority.

stories.headline: Lawmakers from both parties demand Nvidia CEO investigation over alleged China ties
stories.summary: Republicans and Democrats are showing rare unity in calling for investigations into whether Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang compromised national security after reports he had an affair tied to alleged Chinese intelligence efforts to obtain chip technology, though the two parties diverge on whether Trump bears responsibility.

stories.headline: Kennedy family sues to block Trump's proposed arch near Arlington Cemetery
stories.summary: Nine Kennedy family members filed suit warning that President Trump's proposed monumental arch would block sight lines to the Kennedy gravesites and the JFK Eternal Flame at Arlington National Cemetery.

stories.headline: Senate advances bipartisan permitting and energy infrastructure bill
stories.summary: The Senate moved a major infrastructure and energy permitting reform bill closer to passage Tuesday night as part of a busy lame-duck session agenda.

stories.headline: Democrats weigh pushing the National Popular Vote Compact after sweeping swing-state wins
stories.summary: Having won unified control of Pennsylvania, Wisconsin and Michigan, Democrats are debating whether to back the National Popular Vote Compact, a move that could let them bypass the Electoral College in presidential elections.

stories.headline: Fed governor signals big rate hike as inflation runs hot
stories.summary: Federal Reserve governor Christopher Waller's comments are seen as the latest sign the central bank is preparing another interest rate increase as inflation persists, complicating the political picture for Fed Chair Kevin Warsh heading into a new Democratic Congress.

US politics.gaps: No outlet-specific recent coverage could be confirmed from Cook Political Report or NOTUS within the last 24-48 hours; search results for both outlets returned only older stories (Cook Political Report's midterm forecasts, NOTUS's earlier Hegseth coverage), so they are omitted from the ranked list. Politico, NYT, WSJ and The Guardian were limited to the feed items provided since they block web search.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage across tech and AI outlets is dominated by Anthropic's blockbuster Nasdaq IPO and Nvidia's escalating corporate crisis tied to CEO Jensen Huang's alleged entanglement with a Chinese spy, alongside a fast-moving AI model arms race (Gemini 4 Carbon vs. Claude Fable 5.2) and new regulatory moves in New York, the EU and UK targeting AI safety and platform design.

stories.headline: Anthropic prices IPO at up to $1.4 trillion valuation, founders to cash out $250M each
stories.summary: Anthropic set an IPO price range of $70-$78 per share, targeting a fully diluted valuation of up to $1.404 trillion, with Google, Nvidia, Microsoft, AMD, Broadcom, Micron and TSMC agreeing to buy $26 billion of stock in a concurrent private placement; each of the seven co-founders is expected to sell shares worth roughly $250 million. Bloomberg and the FT report bankers are now considering pushing the valuation even higher, to $1.5 trillion or more, citing robust investor demand, while trading is expected to begin on Nasdaq around November 19.

stories.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang scandal escalates into a full-blown corporate governance crisis
stories.summary: Reports that a woman identified by U.S. intelligence as a Chinese spy had ties to CEO Jensen Huang dating back to 2023 have rattled Nvidia, with TechCrunch noting governance experts say they have never seen anything like the unfolding fallout, and Nvidia shares falling for a second straight day. Taiwan's media and public, per WSJ, are reassessing their devotion to Huang as the island's AI-chip hometown hero amid the scandal.

stories.headline: OpenAI's quarterly revenue hits $10 billion but losses balloon even as it trails Anthropic
stories.summary: OpenAI grew quarterly revenue 50 percent to $10 billion on enterprise sales, but adjusted operating losses climbed to $10.9 billion even as rival Anthropic reported faster revenue growth in its own IPO filings. Techmeme and Bloomberg both flagged the figure as a sign of surging but costly AI enterprise adoption just as Anthropic heads toward its own Wall Street debut.

stories.headline: New York's AI safety law takes effect, forcing OpenAI and Anthropic into new disclosure regime
stories.summary: New York is preparing to enforce its sweeping AI safety law, which requires major developers like OpenAI and Anthropic to register, disclose safety practices, and report critical incidents or face fines.

stories.headline: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Carbon, undercutting Anthropic's new Claude models on price
stories.summary: Google made Gemini 4 Carbon generally available just two weeks after unveiling it, with the model ranking first on several benchmarks though Anthropic's newly launched Fable 5.2 has since pulled ahead on some measures. VentureBeat reported Carbon's API pricing undercuts Claude Fable 5.2 and Opus 5.5, intensifying an unusually fast-paced model release cycle between the two labs.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches office suite with Sheets and Whiteboards, challenging Microsoft and Google
stories.summary: Anthropic is expanding Claude with new Sheets, Whiteboards and Interactive Connector tools that let partners like Adobe and Atlassian embed their apps inside Claude, with Meeting notes coming soon, pushing the AI company into productivity-suite territory just ahead of its IPO.

stories.headline: SoftBank takes $3.7B hit after canceling massive turbine reservations for AI power
stories.summary: SoftBank had reserved more than 13 gigawatts of turbines, equivalent to six Hoover Dams, to power AI infrastructure, but took a $3.7 billion earnings hit mostly from canceled reservations, according to the Wall Street Journal, underscoring growing strain in AI energy buildouts.

stories.headline: xAI's Grok Build coding agent exposed tens of thousands of confidential projects
stories.summary: A researcher found that roughly 35,000 apps built with xAI's Grok Build coding agent were left wide open to anyone searching for them, exposing confidential information including material belonging to SpaceX.

Tech & AI.gaps: Rest of World, Wired, The Economist, and The Guardian had no AI/tech-specific stories distinct from the feed items provided in the last 24-48 hours; Platformer, The Information and VentureBeat are largely covering the same Anthropic IPO and Gemini 4 Carbon stories already listed above rather than distinct angles.

Energy.overview: Coverage is dominated by the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, with outlets focused on the US absence from the talks, a sharp drop in climate-finance pledges, and tensions over fossil-fuel reliance. A parallel major theme is the fallout from the US midterm elections, as energy affordability and data-center backlash reshape state-level utility and climate policy, alongside rising winter heating costs and Middle East energy-security risks.

stories.headline: What to Know About COP31
stories.summary: World leaders are gathering in Antalya, Turkey for the 31st UN climate summit, while the United States again skips the talks after Trump withdrew the country from the Paris Agreement and the UNFCCC.

stories.headline: Analysis: Climate-finance pledges fall 70% as countries meet at COP31
stories.summary: Public climate-finance pledges to help developing nations have collapsed by more than 70% this year, falling to roughly $11.7bn annually from around $40bn as the US withdraws and European donors cut aid budgets.

stories.headline: Burnham's North Sea Drilling Dilemma Risks UK Climate Leadership
stories.summary: A majority of UK cabinet ministers back drilling at the Rosebank North Sea oil field, with a decision expected only after COP31 concludes, turning the project into a test of Prime Minister Andy Burnham's climate credibility.

stories.headline: How Democrats' midterm sweep will rewire energy and data center policy
stories.summary: A sweeping Democratic midterm win has shifted control over large-load policy, utility capital recovery and data-center development to newly elected governors and commissions in states including Texas, Georgia and Wisconsin.

stories.headline: Inside the 'pressure cooker': Electric utility regulators gather in wake of electoral earthquake
stories.summary: State utility regulators meeting at a NARUC conference described newly elected officials and angry ratepayers as upending long-standing approaches to rate cases and grid investment.

stories.headline: Heating Costs Will Rise 7% on Average This Winter
stories.summary: US households face average winter heating cost increases of 7%, with heating-oil users seeing roughly 70% higher bills because the Iran conflict has sharply reduced fuel supply.

stories.headline: Adnoc Gas Still Evaluating Options to Bypass Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Adnoc Gas's CEO says the company is still examining ways to cut reliance on the Strait of Hormuz, including a potential LNG export facility on the UAE's east coast.

stories.headline: PPL increases capital plan to $25B with proposed Kentucky gas plant
stories.summary: PPL is expanding its capital spending plan to $25 billion and proposing a new Kentucky gas plant to meet projected data-center-driven load growth of roughly 50 GW across Kentucky and Pennsylvania.

Energy.gaps: No recent (last 48h) coverage was found from Argus Media or E&E News on this topic; the only E&E News item located was several months old.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage across outlets is dominated by the fallout from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's admitted affair with a woman US officials suspect of Chinese espionage ties, which state media, Asian outlets and Western papers are all covering from different angles, alongside China's October trade data showing the annual surplus has again topped $1 trillion. Business and tech outlets are also tracking a reshaping auto/EV landscape (VW's China strategy reversal, BYD's export lead) and continued US-China tech-restriction maneuvering, while Hong Kong and Macau national-security prosecutions keep generating cross-border diplomatic friction.

stories.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair fuels 'Chinese spy' firestorm
stories.summary: State-run Global Times ran a series of pieces defending Huang and accusing US media and lawmakers of weaponizing unproven 'Chinese spy' claims against the Nvidia CEO for political and protectionist ends, while China's foreign ministry dismissed the allegations as a groundless smear. The controversy triggered a board investigation at Nvidia, a stock selloff, and calls from US lawmakers for tougher export controls on AI chips to China.

stories.headline: China's trade surplus tops $1 trillion for the year
stories.summary: China's October exports rose 35.2% year-on-year while imports jumped 41.6%, pushing the cumulative 2026 trade surplus past $1 trillion despite a strengthening yuan and growing Western scrutiny of the imbalance. Analysts noted AI-chip demand and EV exports are driving the surplus, while imports were lifted by higher energy and commodity prices rather than a genuine domestic demand recovery.

stories.headline: US lawmakers push tougher China export controls amid Nvidia scrutiny
stories.summary: Momentum is building in the newly Democrat-controlled Congress to attach a slate of stricter China export-control measures to the annual defense bill, with the Nvidia spy controversy adding political fuel. Nikkei Asia separately reported Washington extended a suspension of expanded blacklist rules on Chinese firms to January 10, prolonging the trade truce even as scrutiny intensifies.

stories.headline: Volkswagen overhauls 'In China, For China' strategy
stories.summary: Volkswagen is revising its localized China strategy as the German automaker struggles with a sharp sales downturn in the world's largest car market.

stories.headline: Macau jails pro-democracy ex-lawmaker Au Kam-san for 12.5 years
stories.summary: The US said it strongly condemns the sentencing of former Macau lawmaker and pro-democracy activist Au Kam San, the territory's first national-security conviction of this kind, with his wife calling the verdict a political judgment. The case adds to a wave of national-security prosecutions across Hong Kong and Macau, including the recent 10-year sentence given to activist Joshua Wong.

stories.headline: Chinese AI labs struggle to poach Silicon Valley talent
stories.summary: Chinese AI startups like MiniMax and Moonshot are opening US outposts to recruit top engineers, but face steep pay gaps, lower prestige, and national-security tensions that make luring talent from OpenAI and Anthropic difficult.

stories.headline: BYD retains lead in China's NEV exports as Tesla's share rises
stories.summary: BYD exported 164,679 new-energy vehicles in October, holding the top spot with a 28.3% export share even as its total fell from September, while Tesla's export share climbed to 10.1%. A companion report showed Tesla dropping out of the domestic retail top 10 as Xiaomi, Xpeng and Great Wall gained ground.

China.gaps: No recent coverage found for Sixth Tone, China Media Project, Yicai Global, CGTN, China Daily, or Xinhua in the search results; Reuters, AP, and NYT could not be searched directly and no relevant feed items from them were provided.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Gulf and Middle East outlets are dominated by the US-Iran standoff over the Strait of Hormuz and Iran's refusal to surrender enriched uranium, alongside renewed Gaza violence, Russia-Ukraine-US peace talks hosted in Abu Dhabi, and the COP31 climate summit in Turkey. Business coverage centers on Dubai's first IPO of 2026 and strong UAE corporate tax receipts.

stories.headline: US and Iran continue tit-for-tat strikes over Strait of Hormuz control
stories.summary: The US and Iran are waging an escalating battle over the Strait of Hormuz, with both sides striking islands in the waterway in recent days even as mediators try to prevent full-scale escalation. The New Arab reported that despite Trump calling the war 'effectively over,' attacks on tankers in the strait are continuing almost daily, with at least 11 ships hit in a single week according to UKMTO.

stories.headline: Iran vows no enriched nuclear material will leave the country
stories.summary: Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran will not allow even a single particle of its enriched nuclear material to leave the country and warned of consequences if there is further escalation. Ynetnews reported Israeli and Western intelligence estimate the stockpile at about 450 kilograms, directly complicating a Qatari-brokered deal reportedly worth $8 billion to reopen Hormuz.

stories.headline: Israeli strikes kill Palestinians in Gaza, including children
stories.summary: Israeli forces killed at least seven Palestinians in Gaza, including a father and his 13-year-old son, according to local health officials, with the Israeli military saying it struck 'terror operatives.' Times of Israel and Haaretz separately reported additional fatal strikes over the past days, including a 20-year-old Gaza Sports Club goalkeeper killed days after playing in a cup for slain athletes, per Al Jazeera.

stories.headline: Russia, Ukraine and US hold second day of peace talks in Abu Dhabi
stories.summary: Russian, Ukrainian and US officials resumed a second day of talks in Abu Dhabi aimed at advancing peace negotiations, underscoring the UAE's growing role as a diplomatic venue for major-power mediation.

stories.headline: Dubai's DIP Holding surges on debut, ending UAE's year-long IPO drought
stories.summary: DIP Holding shares jumped as much as 7% on their Dubai Financial Market debut after a $529 million IPO marked the UAE's first listing of 2026, following a slowdown in regional IPO activity tied to the Iran conflict. Gulf News reported the offering was oversubscribed roughly four times, with the stock climbing to Dh1.19 from its Dh1.12 issue price.

stories.headline: UAE corporate tax revenue jumps a third to Dh46.5bn in 2025
stories.summary: The UAE's corporate tax revenue rose sharply in 2025, a sign of resilient business activity in the emirates even amid regional conflict and oil-market volatility stemming from the Iran war.

stories.headline: UN chief warns climate crisis is 'outrunning us' at COP31 in Turkey
stories.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres told world leaders at the COP31 summit in Antalya that the slow pace of international climate action is falling dangerously behind the scale of the crisis. Turkish President Erdogan told the same summit that developed countries must do far more to finance climate measures, while The National reported the UAE sent a high-level delegation to the talks.

stories.headline: US Treasury Secretary Bessent relocated to military base after Iranian threats
stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has moved from his Washington residence to a US military base following threats linked to Iran, according to sources, highlighting how the Hormuz standoff is reverberating in Washington.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Could not find distinct recent lead stories from Arab News, Arabian Business, AGBI, Zawya, Saudi Gazette, Al Arabiya English, Asharq Al-Awsat (beyond feed items), and Reuters/AP/FT/NYT/The Economist/BBC beyond the feed items provided, as these outlets either block search or yielded no new relevant results in this period.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage across these outlets centers on South Africa's fraught political and economic recalibration after municipal elections and US trade exclusions, alongside major African elections (South Sudan), resource governance disputes in the DRC, and Nigeria's deepening power crisis. Business and fintech outlets are tracking continent-wide economic diversification, from Ghana's jobs push to South African fintech expansion beyond payments.

stories.headline: US shows it can't afford to lose South Africa despite AGOA, G20 exclusions
stories.summary: Despite South Africa's exclusion from AGOA trade benefits and the G20 presidency, major US tech firms and government departments are intensifying engagement with Cape Town's tech sector, underscoring Washington's reluctance to fully disengage economically.

stories.headline: The ANC pays the price of holding on to power
stories.summary: Africa Confidential, a subscription newsletter, reports that South Africa's ANC is losing dominance after recent municipal elections, with established political brokers rather than young activists driving the realignment inside Ramaphosa's national coalition.

stories.headline: South Sudan vote: UN warns political transition must hold beyond polling day
stories.summary: With South Sudan's first national election since independence just six weeks away, the UN is cautioning that the real test will be whether the political transition holds after votes are cast.

stories.headline: Congo says US minerals deal should be judged by projects, not signed deals
stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo pressed Washington to deliver concrete investment under their strategic minerals partnership, arguing that success should be judged by actual projects rather than signed agreements, amid a separate crackdown on illegal copper and cobalt mining.

stories.headline: Electricity-starved Nigerians hard hit by El Niño as blackout worsens
stories.summary: Falling gas supply and reduced hydropower output linked to El Niño have worsened blackouts on Nigeria's national grid, hitting households and small businesses hard just as officials warn of extreme heat.

stories.headline: Ghana's $9bn jobs bet: Five questions ahead of the 2027 budget
stories.summary: President John Mahama is trying to turn Ghana's post-bailout recovery into an industrial jobs boom, but a reckoning in gold trading and a looming debt wall could complicate his $9bn jobs pledge.

stories.headline: South Africa: DA doesn't dictate to others on candidates, says Helen Zille as coalition talks start
stories.summary: As coalition negotiations begin across South Africa's hung municipal councils, DA figure Helen Zille is rejecting demands to abandon her Johannesburg mayoral bid, insisting rivals cannot dictate the choice of mayor.

stories.headline: South Africa's fintechs chase a lucrative opportunity beyond payments
stories.summary: South African fintechs including Yoco, Optasia and Paymenow are moving beyond payments into merchant financing, using transaction data and digital platforms to serve consumers and small businesses.

Africa.gaps: The Continent's site offered no distinct dated articles from the last 48 hours beyond general site information, so no specific story could be confirmed there. No recent items were available for Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT or WSJ, as these outlets block search and no feed items were supplied for them.

Media.overview: Media-industry coverage over the past two days is dominated by consolidation fallout from the Paramount–Warner Bros. Discovery/Skydance merger, with buyout-driven staff exodus at CNN and CBS News and leadership tensions between Bari Weiss and Mark Thompson. Outlets are also tracking a major British press-freedom fight over a UK celebrity sex-abuse scandal, the fate of The New York Times' blockbuster copyright suit against OpenAI/Microsoft, BBC's ongoing Trump defamation battle, and continued structural stress on local journalism funding and audience trust in AI.

stories.headline: The CBS-CNN Cashout
stories.summary: Skydance's buyout offers at CNN and CBS News, issued as the company chases $6 billion in post-merger savings, are triggering an exodus of veteran staffers with unintended consequences for management as a deeper round of layoffs looms.

stories.headline: What Could the Times Buy With Its A.I. Bucks?
stories.summary: With reply briefs due November 20 in the NYT's copyright suit against OpenAI and Microsoft, lawyers tell Puck a nine- or ten-figure settlement is likely, which could fund further M&A for the Times and reshape licensing leverage across the publishing industry.

stories.headline: David Walliams scandal roils British TV industry amid injunction fight and libel-law debate
stories.summary: Fallout from allegations against David Walliams has spread through UK entertainment, with Jonathan Ross explaining a controversial joke about him, comedian Lucy Beaumont saying she fears industry blacklisting for speaking out, and WSJ noting the case has reignited debate over Britain's strict libel laws.

stories.headline: BBC Fails to Get Trump's $10 Billion Defamation Lawsuit Dismissed
stories.summary: A judge rejected the BBC's bid to toss President Trump's $10 billion defamation suit, ruling the broadcaster had created something materially different from what was actually said in the speech at issue.

stories.headline: ITV's Sky Sale 'Progressing as Planned' as Ad Slump Forces Content Cuts
stories.summary: ITV CEO Carolyn McCall said the broadcaster's sale of its Media & Entertainment business to Sky remains on track even as weaker UK advertiser demand has forced fourth-quarter content-spend cuts.

stories.headline: Entertainment 360 Acquires Brigade, a Management Firm Rich in Substackers
stories.summary: A Hollywood talent and management company has bought Brigade, bringing Substack writers and podcast hosts under the same management roof as movie stars, a sign of creator-economy consolidation with traditional entertainment.

stories.headline: Canada Renews Local Journalism Initiative and Extends Journalism Tax Credit
stories.summary: Canada's proposed federal budget extends the country's journalism tax credit by $501 million and expands eligibility to audio and audiovisual news, a lifeline framed by backers as essential to local journalism's survival.

stories.headline: Newsmax's Trump Troubles
stories.summary: Nielsen data obtained by Status shows Newsmax's 25-54 demo audience plunged 33% year-over-year after the midterms, even as the network's hosts turned on Fox News rivals amid the GOP's election wipeout.

Media.gaps: Could not independently verify current coverage from FT or CJR beyond the feed items provided; The Guardian item in the feed was unrelated to media-industry topics, though Deadline's reporting indicates The Guardian is separately pursuing a press-freedom story alongside ITV News.
